parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for pure ESM Node.js files, manual argv behavior, local imports, /output placement, and separate renderer modes for default markdown, tables, and extra.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated CLI probing and Markdown probing while also owning final integration. Children independently explored behavior and wrote implementation files in the same /output workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent ultimately hand-built a dependency-free renderer and parser. A child implementation path instead wrapped the reference executable through child_process, and another child also wrote competing modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After discovering mixed /output contents, the parent interrupted children, rewrote test11.mjs, and deleted child-produced wrapper and module files before delivering a parent-owned pure-JS tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran sample and edge-case comparisons against the executable and got local checks passing, but did not exhaustively match Python-Markdown behavior.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation completed at 25/70, showing the pure-JS renderer remained incomplete despite complying better with the pure-JavaScript constraint.

serial.requirements: The serial agent saw the same prompt requirements but prioritized exact byte parity with the executable over the prohibition on Python embedding or calling the reference executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, parser implementation, bridge implementation, verification, and final packaging; there were no child agents or cross-agent ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial solution implemented argv parsing locally but routed Markdown rendering through markdownBridge.mjs, which used node:child_process to call /workspace/dataset/test11_executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial deliverable was internally coherent and packaged as test11.mjs plus lib modules, but its core rendering path depended on the forbidden executable bridge.
serial.verification: The serial run verified byte parity against the same executable it called at runtime, so the checks confirmed wrapper behavior rather than an independent JavaScript reimplementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation completed at 0/70 because the submitted code was task-invalid under the pure JavaScript and no-Python-executable constraints.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the pure ESM and no external/Python-wrapper constraints and later described a pure local-import renderer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the same prompt but its final deliverable explicitly used child_process to call the reference executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel tried to satisfy the pure-JS reimplementation requirement; serial optimized for byte parity in a way that violated that requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split CLI and Markdown exploration across child agents while the parent kept final integration authority.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one agent handle probing, implementation, verification, and delivery without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping implementation ownership in /output; serial avoided coordination boundaries but also lacked an independent check against its invalid bridge choice.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children operated with overlapping deliverable scope; one returned a wrapper design that conflicted with the parent's pure-JS path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff boundary; the same actor chose the wrapper path and kept that interface coherent internally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a cross-agent conflict to adjudicate, while serial had a single coherent but task-invalid design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered local parser and Markdown-renderer modules in a pure-JS hierarchy.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered parser modules plus markdownBridge.mjs, which delegated rendering to the packaged executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation paths diverged at rendering: incomplete local reimplementation versus forbidden runtime bridge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received a child result, inspected the workspace, rejected the wrapper path, interrupted children, and took over finalization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child results to retrieve or merge and finalized after local parity checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a visible result lifecycle with adjudication and cleanup; serial had a linear result path with no join risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple agents wrote competing /output files, including the required test11.mjs, then the parent rewrote the entrypoint and deleted child-produced wrapper files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent file tree from one actor; there was no cross-agent overwrite or cleanup episode.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred a shared-workspace deliverable replacement; serial had no coordination collision but retained the invalid bridge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran many comparisons and smoke checks after taking over the tree, but the checks covered selected behavior and missed hidden Markdown gaps.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran parity checks against the executable bridge and therefore verified that the wrapper matched the same program it invoked.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was imperfect but exercised its own JS implementation; serial verification was circular for the bridge design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and about 902 agent seconds, but did not time out and delivered after cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and about 393 agent seconds, also without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and coordination budget resolving competing work; serial closed faster by choosing the invalid executable bridge.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail split. The important difference is score and compliance path: parallel delivered a pure-JS renderer that passed 25 of 70 cases but missed hidden Markdown behavior, while serial delivered a runtime bridge to the reference executable and therefore failed all 70 official cases despite local parity checks.
parallel_contributors: Parent rejected the child wrapper and preserved a pure-JS implementation path, which explains why some cases passed.
The hand-written Markdown renderer remained incomplete against the hidden official suite, leaving the parallel solution failed.
serial_contributors: Serial used child_process to invoke the reference executable from markdownBridge.mjs, violating the pure-JavaScript/no-Python-executable requirement.
Serial verification compared the wrapper against the same executable it called, so local parity did not test compliance with the migration constraint.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel attempted a partial JavaScript reimplementation of Python-Markdown behavior; serial avoided reimplementation by runtime delegation.
Parallel local tests covered representative features but not enough of the official suite.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative explanation for a both-fail score gap, not an exclusive root cause or a discordant outcome explanation.
